title: Microsoft plans to unveil next-generation AI chip in September
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Microsoft plans to unveil its next-generation Maia 300 artificial-intelligence accelerator as early as September, The Information reported, signaling an expansion of the company’s custom-silicon strategy for Azure.

The chip would follow Maia 200, introduced in January and manufactured on Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company’s 3-nanometer process. Maia 200 contains 100 billion transistors and emphasizes on-chip SRAM, high-bandwidth memory and low-precision computing for large-scale model inference. Microsoft described that processor as its most cost-efficient inference platform, claiming a 30% improvement in performance per dollar over existing systems.

Maia 300 is expected to increase Microsoft’s internal deployment of proprietary accelerators and reduce its dependence on Nvidia’s costly, supply-constrained graphics processors. The Information said Microsoft is negotiating with TSMC for manufacturing capacity covering 300,000 Maia 300 chips for delivery in 2027, with ambitions exceeding one million units. Maia division head Andrew Wall disputed the reported production numbers.

Developing chips internally gives Microsoft tighter control over hardware, networking, compilers and AI software, allowing the company to optimize the Azure stack for specific workloads. It also places Microsoft in direct competition with Google’s Tensor Processing Units and Amazon Web Services’ Trainium accelerators.

The commercial challenge extends beyond silicon performance. Microsoft must secure advanced packaging, high-bandwidth memory, power capacity and software compatibility while achieving high utilization across Azure. Customer adoption will also matter: the company reportedly hopes to attract major global model developers, including Anthropic. A September unveiling would mark an important milestone, but volume deployment, economics and developer support will determine Maia 300’s strategic impact.
